notes: arrivalMinutes is measured from 00:58:53 UTC. Merrifield et al. (2005) give travel times from 00:59 UTC (whole minutes), so for those stations arrivalUTC = 00:59 + travel time and arrivalMinutes = travel time + 7 s. Coordinates are not given in Merrifield 2005 or Nagarajan 2006. They come from the present-day UHSLC station metadata (https://uhslc.soest.hawaii.edu/data/meta.geojson) or the PSMSL station list (https://psmsl.org/data/obtaining/rlr.monthly.data/filelist.txt), as named in coordSource. Thai coordinates are from Tsuji et al. 2006, Table 2. Hillarys (W. Australia, 115.74E) is excluded because it falls outside the 112.5E bound.

stations.name: Port Blair
stations.source: Bilham, R., Engdahl, E. R., Feldl, N., Satyabala, S. P. (2005), Partial and complete rupture of the Indo-Andaman plate boundary 1847-2004, Seismological Research Letters (author draft, 4 March 2005)
stations.note: UNCERTAIN. Source: the Port Blair gauge 'is reported to have recorded initial subsidence of the harbor (or rise in sea level) at 07:14 Indian time' (IST = UTC+5:30, so 01:44 UTC). Eyewitnesses reported a tsunami 15-30 min after 5 min of shaking. The authors say they are 'uncertain ... whether the initial rise ... signifies the first arrival of the tsunami or subsidence of the harbor'. Nagarajan et al. 2006 say the SOI Port Blair gauge was under repair, so this preliminary report is unpublished data. Use only as a soft check.

stations.name: Cocos Islands
stations.source: Merrifield, M. A., et al. (2005), Tide gauge observations of the Indian Ocean tsunami, December 26, 2004, Geophys. Res. Lett., 32, L09603, doi:10.1029/2005GL022610 (Table 1)
stations.note: Travel time 02:18 from 00:59 UTC to the first water-level change. First crest 0.33 m. 1-min sampling. Atoll, inner lagoon.

stations.name: Kuraburi
stations.source: Tsuji, Y., et al. (2006), The 2004 Indian tsunami in Thailand: Surveyed runup heights and tide gauge records, Earth Planets Space, 58, 223-232, doi:10.1186/BF03353382 (Section 5, Fig. 3a, Table 2)
stations.coordSource: Tsuji et al. 2006 Table 2: 98 deg 22.613' E, 9 deg 13.503' N
stations.note: Source: 'the first wave withdrew at 10:32' local Thai time (UTC+7, per the paper's '00:58:53 UTC (07:58 in Thai local time)'). First arrival is a withdrawal (trough), with the minimum at 10:58 and the crest at 11:12. Timing caveat: on the same chart the recorded tide was 'delayed by 12 minutes' against the predicted tide, so the true arrival may differ by about 12 min. Paper-chart float gauge.

stations.note: Table 2 arrival time (AT, UTC). First-wave amplitude 64 cm. Float gauge, digitised at 5-6 min. Bilham et al. 2005 independently give 09:06 local (IST), which is 03:36 UTC.

missing: Somalia: no tide gauge record found in the sources read.

Mauritius: at Port Louis the 'travel time' 06:43-07:47 is a data gap and at Rodrigues 05:41+ is the last transmitted data before the station was destroyed (Merrifield 2005), so neither is a usable arrival. Reunion: no open-access arrival time found (Rabinovich & Thomson 2007, PAGEOPH, is paywalled and was not read).
Western Australia: Hillarys (Merrifield 2005, 06:29 travel time) is at 115.74E, outside the lon bound.
Ko Taphao Noi (Phuket): the gauge record exists (Tsuji 2006) but no arrival time is stated in the text. The chart clock was 11 min off when visited.

Not included but available in the same tables: Diego Garcia (Merrifield 04:49 travel time, i.e. 05:48 UTC; Nagarajan's table says 0448 UTC, which looks like a transcription of the travel time), Sibolga (01:21 travel time), Belawan (00:41), Paradip (0330 UTC), Mormugao (0654 UTC), Okha (0906 UTC).
